title: Why Seoul Turned a Downtown Highway Back Into a Stream
mediaSource: Seoul Cheonggyecheon before after elevated highway restoration stream

scenes.title: There used to be a stream under this downtown highway
scenes.narration: Today Cheonggyecheon is a popular walking stream, but for decades the waterway was hidden beneath roads and an elevated highway.

scenes.title: Rapid growth covered the water with roads
scenes.narration: As Seoul expanded, sections of Cheonggyecheon were covered and roads were built above it, turning the corridor into car-centered infrastructure.

scenes.title: In 2003 the highway began coming down
scenes.narration: Concerns about aging structures and the downtown environment led Seoul to remove the elevated road and restore the stream.

scenes.title: Water returned in 2005
scenes.narration: The restoration was completed in 2005, replacing traffic infrastructure with a pedestrian-friendly urban waterway.

scenes.title: It also changed the local urban climate
scenes.narration: Official monitoring found changes in airflow and lower temperatures around parts of the restored corridor.

scenes.title: A road became water again
scenes.narration: Cheonggyecheon became one of Seoul's best-known examples of transforming car infrastructure back into public urban space.
